fields.summary: Jesus sends out the Twelve and feeds five thousand, and Peter says who Jesus is. Jesus speaks of the cross, is changed in appearance on the mountain, frees a boy from a spirit, and sets out for Jerusalem; a Samaritan village turns Jesus away.

fields.title: Luke 10
fields.body_html:
Seventy-two sent ahead in pairs

1After this the Lord appointed seventy-two others as well. He sent them out in pairs ahead of him, to every town and place he was going to visit. 2He told them, “There is a great harvest, but only a few workers. So plead with the Lord of the harvest to send workers out to bring in his harvest. 3Go on your way. I am sending you out like lambs among wolves. 4Take no money bag, no pack and no sandals, and do not stop to greet anyone on the way. 5Whatever house you go into, begin by saying, ‘Peace be on this household.’ 6If someone there is a person of peace, your peace will stay with that person. If not, it will come back to you. 7Stay in that one house, eating and drinking whatever they give you, since a worker has earned their pay. Do not keep changing from one house to another. 8Whenever a town takes you in, eat whatever food they put in front of you. 9Heal those in it who are sick, and tell the people, ‘The kingdom of God has drawn near to you.’ 10But if you go into a town where the people do not welcome you, go out into its streets and say, 11‘Against you we wipe off even the dust of your town that has stuck to our feet. All the same, be sure of this: the kingdom of God has come near.’ 12I tell you, on that day Sodom will be better off than that town.

13How terrible for you, Chorazin! How terrible for you, Bethsaida! If the mighty deeds that were done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, their people would long ago have sat down in sackcloth and ashes and repented. 14But at the judgment Tyre and Sidon will be better off than you. 15And you, Capernaum, will you be raised as high as heaven? No, you will be brought down to Hades.

16Anyone who listens to you listens to me. Anyone who turns you away turns me away, and anyone who turns me away turns away the one who sent me.”

The seventy-two come back rejoicing

17The seventy-two came back full of joy. “Lord,” they said, “when we use your name, even the demons obey us!” 18He told them, “I watched Satan fall from heaven like a flash of lightning. 19I have given you authority to trample snakes and scorpions underfoot, and authority over all the enemy’s power. Nothing at all will be able to hurt you. 20But do not be glad because the spirits obey you. Be glad instead that your names stand written in heaven.”

Hidden from the wise, shown to little children

21At that very time Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, “I praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have kept these things hidden from the wise and the clever, and have made them known to little children. Yes, Father, for this is what seemed good to you. 22My Father has put all things into my hands. Who the Son is, only the Father knows; and who the Father is, only the Son knows, along with anyone to whom the Son is willing to make him known.”

23Then he turned to the disciples and said to them alone, “Blessed are the eyes that are seeing what you see. 24I tell you, many prophets and kings longed to see the things you are seeing, yet never saw them; they longed to hear the things you are hearing, yet never heard them.”

Who is my neighbor?

25Then an expert in the law stood up to put Jesus to the test. “Teacher,” he said, “what do I have to do to inherit eternal life?” 26Jesus answered him, “What stands written in the law? What do you read there?” 27He answered, “‘You are to love the Lord your God with your whole heart, your whole soul, your whole strength and your whole mind,’ and ‘your neighbor as you love yourself.’” 28Jesus told him, “Your answer is right. Do this, and you will live.”

29But the man wanted to show that he was in the right, so he asked Jesus, “And who counts as my neighbor?” 30Jesus took up the question and said, “A man was on his way down from Jerusalem to Jericho when robbers set on him. They tore off his clothes, gave him a beating, and went off and left him lying there half dead. 31It so happened that a priest was traveling down by that same road. He saw the man, but went past him, keeping to the far side. 32A Levite did the same. He came to the spot, saw him, and went past on the far side. 33Then a Samaritan, who was on a journey, came to where the man lay. When he saw him, his heart went out to him. 34He went over to him, poured oil and wine on his wounds and bound them up. Then he lifted him onto his own animal, took him to an inn, and looked after him. 35The next day he took out two denarii and handed them to the innkeeper. ‘Care for him,’ he said, ‘and if you spend anything more, I will pay you back on my return.’ 36Now which of these three, in your view, proved to be a neighbor to the man the robbers attacked?” 37He answered, “The one who was merciful to him.” Jesus told him, “You go, then, and do the same.”

Martha serves, Mary listens

38As they went on their way, Jesus came into a village where a woman named Martha welcomed him as her guest. 39Martha had a sister, Mary, who sat down at Jesus’s feet and kept listening to his words. 40But Martha was being pulled in every direction by all the work of serving. She came up and said, “Lord, does it not matter to you that my sister has left me to do the serving on my own? So tell her to give me a hand.” 41The Lord answered her, “Martha, Martha, you are fretting and in a stir about so many things. 42Yet there is need of few things, or only of one. Mary has picked the good share, and it is not going to be taken from her.”
fields.summary: Jesus sends seventy-two ahead in pairs, and they come back rejoicing. Answering an expert in the law, Jesus tells of a Samaritan who stops to help a wounded man, and at the house of Martha and Mary praises Mary for listening.

fields.title: Luke 11
fields.body_html:
Lord, teach us to pray

1Once Jesus was praying in a certain place. When he had finished, one of his disciples asked him, “Lord, teach us how to pray, the way John taught his own disciples.” 2He said to them, “When you pray, say: ‘Father, may your name be honored as holy. May your kingdom come. 3Each day give us the bread we need. 4Forgive us our sins, since we also forgive all who owe us. And do not bring us into temptation.’”

The friend at midnight

5Then he said to them, “Imagine that one of you has a friend, and you go to his house in the middle of the night and say to him, ‘My friend, lend me three loaves. 6Another friend of mine has come to my house from a journey, and I have nothing to set out for him to eat.’ 7Would that friend call back from inside, ‘Do not trouble me. The door is already shut for the night, and my children are in bed with me. I cannot get up now to hand you anything’? 8I tell you, even if friendship is not enough to get him out of bed to give you the bread, your boldness in asking without shame will get him up, and he will give you as much as you need.

Ask, search, knock

9So I tell you: ask, and God will give to you; search, and you will find; knock, and God will open the door for you. 10For all who ask receive, all who search find, and all who knock have the door opened to them. 11Is there a father among you who would hand his son a snake when the boy asked for a fish? 12Or if he asked for an egg, would he give him a scorpion? 13You are evil, and yet you know how to give your children good gifts. Then how much more will the Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him!”

By the finger of God

14Jesus was driving out a demon that had left a man unable to speak. Once the demon was gone, the man spoke. The crowds were amazed. 15But some of them said, “It is by Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons, that he drives out the demons.” 16Others, wanting to test him, kept asking him for a sign from heaven. 17But he knew what they were thinking, and he said to them, “If a kingdom is torn apart by its own people, it is laid waste, and its houses fall one upon another. 18If Satan too is split against himself, how can his kingdom last? Yet that is what you are saying: that I drive out the demons by Beelzebul. 19And if I drive out the demons by Beelzebul, by whose power do your own people drive them out? So they themselves will be the ones to judge you. 20But suppose it is by God’s finger that I drive the demons out. Then the kingdom of God has already reached you. 21As long as a strong man keeps guard over his own palace with all his weapons, his goods are left in peace. 22But then a man stronger than he is comes against him and wins the fight. He strips away all the armor the strong man was counting on, and shares out the goods he has seized. 23Anyone who does not stand with me stands against me, and anyone who does not help me gather is scattering.

The unclean spirit returns

24When an unclean spirit has left a person, it wanders through dry, empty places looking for a place to rest. When it finds none, it says, ‘I will go back to my house, where I came from.’ 25It arrives and finds the house swept and tidied. 26Then it goes and brings seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they go in and make their home there. In the end that person is worse off than at the start.”

Hearing and keeping God’s word

27While he was saying these things, a woman in the crowd called out to him, “Blessed is the woman who carried you in her womb and fed you at her breasts!” 28But he said, “Even more blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it.”

Something greater than Jonah

29With the crowds pressing in more and more, he began to say, “This generation is an evil one. It looks for a sign, yet the only sign it will be given is the sign of Jonah. 30For just as Jonah was a sign to the people of Nineveh, the Son of Man will be a sign to this generation. 31At the judgment the queen of the South will stand up with the people of this generation and condemn them, because she came from the far ends of the earth to listen to Solomon’s wisdom; and here is something greater than Solomon. 32At the judgment the people of Nineveh will stand up with this generation and condemn it, because they repented when Jonah preached; and here is something greater than Jonah.

Light within

33A lamp, once lit, is not hidden away in a cellar or put under a basket; it is set on a lampstand, where anyone coming in will see its light. 34Your body’s lamp is your eye. If your eye is clear, light fills your whole body as well. If your eye is bad, darkness fills your body too. 35So be careful that the light inside you is not really darkness. 36So if light fills your whole body and no part of it is dark, it will be bright all through, as when a lamp shines on you with its beam.”

The inside of the cup

37As he finished speaking, a Pharisee asked him to eat at his home, and he went in and took his place at the table. 38The Pharisee saw that he had not washed before the meal, and it surprised him. 39But the Lord said to him, “You Pharisees clean the cup and the dish on the outside, but your own insides are full of plunder and wickedness. 40Foolish people! The one who made the outside made the inside as well, did he not? 41Rather, give what is inside as gifts to the poor, and then everything is clean for you.

How terrible for you

42But how terrible for you Pharisees! You set aside for God a tenth even of mint and rue and every kind of garden plant, yet you pass over justice and the love of God. Justice and love are what you should have practiced, while not neglecting the tenth. 43How terrible for you Pharisees! You love to sit in the front seats of the synagogues and to be greeted in the marketplaces. 44How terrible for you! You are like graves with no marker, and the people who walk over them are unaware of it.”

Loads too heavy to carry

45One of the experts in the law responded to him, “Teacher, by saying this you are insulting us as well.” 46He said, “How terrible for you experts in the law too! You pile on people loads that are hard to carry, and you yourselves will not touch those loads with even one of your fingers. 47How terrible for you! You build monuments over the prophets’ graves, yet those prophets died at the hands of your ancestors. 48So you are witnesses, and you give your approval to what your ancestors did: they did the killing, and you do the building. 49That is why the Wisdom of God said, ‘I will send them prophets and apostles. They will kill some of them and hunt down others.’ 50And so the blood of all the prophets shed since the world was founded will be charged to this generation, 51from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who died between the altar and the house of God. Yes, I tell you, this generation will be charged with it. 52How terrible for you experts in the law! You have carried off the key of knowledge. You have not gone in yourselves, and you have stood in the way of those who were going in.”

53When he left that place, the scribes and the Pharisees turned bitterly against him and kept pressing him with questions about many things, 54watching for a chance to trap him by his own words.
fields.summary: Jesus teaches the disciples to pray and urges them to ask, search and knock. Accused of driving out demons by Beelzebul, Jesus speaks of the finger of God and the sign of Jonah, and denounces the Pharisees and the experts in the law at a meal.

fields.title: Luke 12
fields.body_html:
The leaven of the Pharisees

1Meanwhile the crowd had grown to many thousands, so packed that people were stepping on one another. Jesus began to speak, first of all to his disciples: “Watch out for the yeast of the Pharisees. I mean their hypocrisy. 2Everything that is covered up now will be uncovered, and every secret will come out. 3So anything you said in the dark will be heard in broad daylight. Anything you spoke into someone’s ear in a back room will be announced from the tops of the houses.

The one to fear

4My friends, I tell you this: do not be afraid of people who can kill the body but then can do nothing further. 5I will point out the one you should fear. Fear the one who, after the killing is done, has the right to throw you into hell. Yes, I tell you, he is the one to fear. 6You can buy five sparrows for two pennies, can you not? Yet God does not forget a single one of them. 7Why, every hair on your head has been counted. So do not be afraid. You matter more than a great many sparrows.

8I tell you, if anyone openly stands with me in front of others, the Son of Man will stand with that person in front of God’s angels. 9But whoever denies knowing me in front of others will be denied in front of God’s angels. 10Anyone who says something against the Son of Man will be forgiven. But anyone who speaks evil against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven. 11People will bring you before synagogues, rulers and officials. When they do, do not worry over how to answer the charges or what words to use. 12When the moment comes, the Holy Spirit will teach you what you need to say.”

A rich man and his barns

13Someone in the crowd said to him, “Teacher, tell my brother to share our father’s property with me.” 14Jesus answered, “Friend, who made me your judge, or put me in charge of dividing your property?” 15Then he said to them, “Take care! Keep yourselves from every kind of greed. Even when someone has more than enough, life does not come from the things a person owns.” 16Then he told them a parable: “There was a rich man whose land gave a huge harvest. 17He kept turning it over in his mind: ‘What am I to do? I have no place where I can store my harvest.’ 18Then he said, ‘Here is my plan. I will pull down my barns and put up larger ones, and I will gather all my grain and my goods into them. 19Then I will say to myself, “You have plenty of good things put away for years to come. Rest now. Eat, drink, and have a good time.”‘ 20But God said to him, ‘You fool! This very night your life is being asked back from you. And the things you have made ready, whose will they be then?’ 21That is how it is for anyone who piles up wealth for themselves but is not rich in God’s sight.”

Life is more than food

22Then Jesus said to his disciples, “That is why I tell you: stop worrying about your life and what you will eat, or about your body and what you will put on it. 23Life is worth more than food, and the body is worth more than clothing. 24Think about the ravens. They do not plant or harvest. They have no storehouse and no barn. Yet God feeds them. And you are worth far more than birds! 25Which of you can make your life one hour longer by worrying? 26If you cannot manage even something so small, why worry about all the rest? 27Look at how the lilies grow. They do not work hard or spin thread. But I tell you, Solomon himself, in all his glory, never wore anything as fine as one of them. 28If God dresses the wild grass this way, grass that is in the field today and fuel for the oven tomorrow, he will do far more for you. How little faith you have! 29So do not be always looking for what you will eat and what you will drink, and do not be on edge about it. 30These are the things that the nations of the world chase after, but your Father knows that you need them. 31Instead, set your hearts on his kingdom, and you will receive these things besides.

32Do not be afraid, my little flock. Your Father has gladly chosen to give you the kingdom. 33Sell what you own and give the money to people in need. Get yourselves money bags that never wear out, a treasure in heaven that will never run out. No thief can get near it there, and no moth can spoil it. 34Your heart will be wherever your treasure is.

Servants waiting for their master

35Stay ready for work, with your belt tied and your lamp lit. 36Be like people who are waiting for their master to come home from a wedding feast, ready to open the door the moment he arrives and knocks. 37Blessed are those servants whom the master finds awake and watching when he comes. Truly I tell you, he will tie on an apron, seat them at the table, and come and wait on them himself. 38He may come in the middle of the night or even later, but if he finds them ready, those servants are blessed.

39You can be sure of this: if the owner of a house knew the hour when the thief was on his way, he would not let anyone dig through the walls of his house. 40Be ready yourselves, then. The Son of Man is coming at an hour when you do not think he will.”

41Peter asked, “Lord, is this parable meant for us, or are you telling it to everyone?” 42The Lord answered, “Who, then, is the manager who can be trusted and who acts wisely? His master will put him in charge of the other workers in the household, to give them their share of food when it is due. 43Blessed is that servant if his master finds him doing just that when he comes home. 44I tell you truly, he will put him in charge of everything he owns. 45But that servant may think, ‘My master will be a long while yet.’ He may start beating the menservants and the serving girls, and eating and drinking until he is drunk. 46Then his master will arrive on a day the servant does not expect, at an hour he has not guessed. He will cut him to pieces and put him with the unfaithful. 47A servant who knew his master’s wishes but made no preparations and did not carry them out will receive a heavy beating. 48But a servant who did not know, though he did what deserved a beating, will get a lighter one. Much will be asked of everyone who has been given much. And when much has been put in someone’s care, even more will be asked of that person.

Fire on the earth

49I came to set fire to the earth, and how I long for it to be blazing already! 50But first I must go through a baptism, and I am under great strain until it is over! 51Do you suppose that I came to bring peace to the earth? No, I tell you, I came to bring division. 52From now on, a family of five will be split, three against two and two against three. 53Father will turn against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, a woman against her son’s wife and the wife against her husband’s mother.”

Reading the time

54Jesus also said to the crowds, “When you see a cloud coming up in the west, you say straight away, ‘There will be rain,’ and so there is. 55And when the south wind is blowing, you say, ‘A scorching day is coming,’ and so it turns out. 56You hypocrites! You can read the face of the earth and the sky. How is it, then, that you cannot read what this moment means? 57Why can you not decide for yourselves what is right? 58When someone is taking you to court before the magistrate, do your best to settle with them while you are still on the way. If you do not, your accuser may drag you before the judge. The judge may hand you over to the officer, and the officer may throw you into prison. 59I tell you, there will be no way out for you until the very last penny is paid.”
fields.summary: Jesus warns against the leaven of the Pharisees and tells of a rich fool who built bigger barns. The disciples are not to worry but to seek God’s kingdom and to be like servants ready for their master’s return.

fields.title: Luke 13
fields.body_html:
Unless you repent

1At that very time some people there told Jesus about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mingled with the blood of their sacrifices. 2He answered them, “Do you suppose that these Galileans suffered this because they were worse sinners than all the other people of Galilee? 3No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you will all perish as they did. 4Or think of those eighteen who were killed when the tower at Siloam fell on them. Do you suppose they were more guilty than everyone else living in Jerusalem? 5No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you will all perish just as they did.”

A fig tree with no fruit

6Then he told this parable:

“A man had a fig tree growing in his vineyard. He came to look for fruit on it, but found none. 7So he said to the man who tended the vineyard, ‘Three years now I have come to this fig tree looking for fruit, and I never find any. Cut it down! Why should it keep wasting good ground?’ 8The man answered, ‘Sir, let it stand this year too, while I dig around it and work manure into the soil. 9If after that it bears fruit next year, well and good. If it does not, you can have it cut down.’”

A daughter of Abraham set free

10Once, on a Sabbath, Jesus was teaching in one of the local synagogues. 11A woman was there whom a spirit had kept sick for eighteen years. Her back was bent, and she could not stand fully upright. 12When Jesus saw her, he called her over and told her, “Woman, you have been released from your illness.” 13Then he placed his hands on her, and right away she stood up straight and began to give glory to God. 14But the ruler of the synagogue was annoyed that Jesus had healed someone on the Sabbath, and he spoke up and told the crowd, “Work may be done on six days. Come to be healed on any of them, but not on the Sabbath day.” 15The Lord answered him, “You hypocrites! On the Sabbath every one of you unties your ox or your donkey from its stall and takes it out for water, do you not? 16And here is a daughter of Abraham whom Satan has kept tied up for eighteen whole years. Should she not be untied from this bond on the Sabbath day?” 17When he said this, everyone who had set themselves against him was put to shame, while the whole crowd rejoiced at all the glorious things he was doing.

Like a mustard seed, like yeast

18So he said, “What is the kingdom of God like? What picture shall I use for it? 19It is like this: a man took a mustard seed and sowed it in his own garden. It kept growing until it was a tree, and birds of the air came and nested among its branches.”

20Once more he said, “With what shall I compare the kingdom of God? 21It is like yeast. A woman took some and hid it in about 40 pounds of flour, and in time the whole batch rose.”

Strive to enter

22Jesus traveled on from town to town and village to village, teaching, and pressing on toward Jerusalem. 23Someone asked him, “Lord, is it only a few who are being saved?” He said to them, 24“Struggle hard to get in through the narrow door. Many people, I tell you, will look for a way in and will fail. 25When the master of the house has risen and locked the door, you will find yourselves outside. You will knock and call out, ‘Lord, open up for us!’ And his answer to you will be, ‘I do not know you; I do not know where you are from.’ 26Then you will begin to protest, ‘We ate and drank in your company, and it was in our streets that you taught!’ 27But he will tell you, ‘I do not know where you come from. Go away from me, all of you whose work is wrongdoing!’ 28You will weep there and grind your teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and every one of the prophets inside the kingdom of God, and yourselves driven out. 29And others will arrive from east and west, from north and south, and sit down to eat in the kingdom of God. 30Some who are last now will be first, and some who are first now will be last.”

A message for Herod

31At that very time some Pharisees came up to him with a warning: “Get away from here and be on your way, because Herod intends to kill you.” 32He answered them, “Go and tell that fox: ‘Today and tomorrow I cast out demons and carry out cures, and on the third day I finish my course.’ 33But I must go on my way today, tomorrow, and the day after, because it cannot be that a prophet should die anywhere but in Jerusalem. 34Jerusalem, Jerusalem! You kill the prophets and stone the messengers sent to you. How many times I wanted to gather your children, the way a hen keeps her young ones under her wings! But you refused. 35Now your house is left to you. I tell you, you will not see me until the time comes when you say, ‘Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord.’”
fields.summary: Jesus calls all to repent and tells of a fig tree given one more year. On the Sabbath Jesus heals a woman bent over for eighteen years, compares the kingdom to a mustard seed and yeast, urges striving to enter the narrow door, and laments over Jerusalem.

fields.title: Luke 14
fields.body_html:
A Sabbath meal and a man with dropsy

1One Sabbath he went to eat a meal at the house of one of the leading Pharisees, and the people there kept a close eye on him. 2There in front of him was a man whose body was swollen with dropsy. 3Jesus responded by asking the experts in the law and the Pharisees, “Does the law allow healing on the Sabbath, or does it not?” 4But they said nothing. So he took hold of the man, healed him, and sent him on his way. 5Then he said to them, “If one of you had a son or an ox that fell into a well on the Sabbath, would you not pull him out right away?” 6And they had no answer to give to this.

Taking the lowest place

7When he saw how the guests were picking out the places of honor for themselves, he gave them a parable: 8“If you are invited to a wedding feast, do not settle yourself in the place of honor. Someone of higher rank than you may be among the guests, 9and the host who invited you both will come over and say, ‘Give your place to this guest.’ Then, to your shame, you will start down to the lowest place. 10No, when you are invited, go and take the last place at the table, so that when your host comes over he will tell you, ‘Friend, move further up.’ Then everyone eating with you will see the honor you are given. 11For everyone who lifts themselves up will be brought low, and the one who takes the low place will be lifted up.”

Guests who cannot repay

12Then he said to his host as well, “When you put on a lunch or a dinner, do not ask your friends, your brothers and sisters, your relatives, or your wealthy neighbors. They might ask you back, and that would be your repayment. 13Instead, when you hold a feast, ask the poor to come, and those who are maimed, lame, or blind. 14And you will be blessed, for they have no way to pay you back. Your repayment will come at the resurrection of the righteous.”

The dinner the guests refused

15One of the guests at the table heard this and said to him, “Blessed is anyone who will sit at the table in the kingdom of God!” 16He answered him, “Once a man was putting on a large dinner, and he had asked many people to it. 17When the hour of the dinner arrived, he sent his servant out to say to the guests he had asked, ‘Come, it is all ready now.’ 18But all of them alike began to ask to be excused. The first told him, ‘I have bought a piece of land, and I have to go out and look at it. I am asking you to excuse me.’ 19Another said, ‘I have bought five pairs of oxen, and I am on my way to test them. I am asking you to excuse me.’ 20And another said, ‘I have taken a wife, and that is why I am not able to come.’ 21The servant came back and told his master all of this. At that the owner of the house was angry, and he said to his servant, ‘Hurry out into the squares and alleys of the town, and bring the poor, the maimed, the blind, and the lame in here.’ 22Then the servant said, ‘Master, your order has been carried out, and there are still empty places.’ 23The master told the servant, ‘Go out to the country roads and the hedgerows, and press people to come in, so that my house will be full. 24For I tell you all, not a single one of the men I first invited will taste my dinner.’”

Counting the cost of following

25Many crowds were walking along with him. He turned around and said to them, 26“No one can be my disciple who comes to me without hating their father and mother, their wife and children, their brothers and sisters, and even their own life. 27Unless a person carries their own cross and walks behind me, they cannot be my disciple. 28If any of you planned to build a tower, would you not sit down first and add up the expense, to find out whether you could afford to finish it? 29If you lay the foundation and cannot finish the job, everyone who sees it will start to make fun of you. 30They will say, ‘Here is someone who started to build and could not finish.’ 31Or what king sets out to fight another king without first sitting down to weigh whether his 10,000 troops can stand against an enemy who comes with 20,000? 32If he cannot, then while the other king is still a long way off, he will send envoys to ask how peace can be made. 33So it is with you: whoever does not let go of all that they have cannot be my disciple.

Salt that loses its taste

34So salt is a good thing. But if even salt goes flat, how will its flavor be brought back? 35It is no use for the field, or even for the manure heap; people just throw it away. Whoever has ears to hear should listen!”
fields.summary: At a Sabbath meal Jesus heals a man with dropsy and teaches guests to take the lowest place and hosts to invite those who cannot repay. The parable of the great dinner is followed by a call to count the cost of following.

fields.title: Luke 15
fields.body_html:
One sheep out of a hundred

1Tax collectors and sinners, all of them, kept coming near to listen to him. 2But the Pharisees and the scribes complained among themselves. “This man welcomes sinners,” they said, “and even shares meals with them.” 3So Jesus put this parable to them: 4“Which man among you, if he owned a hundred sheep and lost one of them, would not leave the ninety-nine out in the wild country and search for the lost one until he found it? 5And when he finds it, he hoists it onto his shoulders, delighted. 6Back at home, he invites his friends and neighbors over. ‘Celebrate with me,’ he tells them, ‘because the sheep I lost has been found.’ 7In the same way, I tell you, one sinner who repents will bring more joy in heaven than ninety-nine righteous people who have no need to repent.

A coin swept for and found

8Or what woman with ten silver coins, if she lost one of them, would not light a lamp, sweep out her house and hunt for it carefully until she found it? 9When she finds it, she gathers her friends and neighbors. ‘Be glad with me,’ she says, ‘for the coin I had lost is found.’ 10So it is, I tell you: when one sinner repents, there is joy before the angels of God.”

A father and his two sons

11Then he said, “A man had two sons. 12The younger son said to his father, ‘Father, let me have the part of the estate that will come to me.’ So the father split what he had between the two of them. 13Only a few days later the younger son packed up everything he owned and traveled to a far country, where he threw his property away on a reckless way of life. 14When he had used up everything, a terrible famine struck that whole land, and he began to go without. 15So he went and attached himself to one of the people of that country, and the man sent him out into his fields to look after pigs. 16He wished he could fill himself up with the carob pods the pigs were eating, but no one gave him a thing. 17At last he saw his situation clearly. ‘So many of my father’s hired workers have more bread than they can eat,’ he said, ‘while I am dying of hunger here! 18I will get up and go back to my father, and I will tell him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight. 19I do not deserve to be called your son any longer. Take me on as one of your hired workers.”‘ 20So he set off and went back to his father. His father caught sight of him while he was still far away, and his heart went out to him. He ran to meet him, embraced him and kissed him warmly. 21His son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight. I do not deserve to be called your son any longer.’ 22But the father said to his servants, ‘Hurry! Bring out the finest robe and dress him in it. Give him a ring for his hand and sandals for his feet. 23Fetch the calf we have been fattening and slaughter it. Let us eat and celebrate, 24for my son here was dead, and now he lives again. He was lost, and now he has been found.’ And the celebration began.

The older son

25All this time the older son had been out in the field. On his way back, as he came close to the house, the sound of music and dancing reached him. 26He called over one of the servants and asked him what this could mean. 27‘Your brother is home,’ the servant told him, ‘and your father has slaughtered the fattened calf, because his son has come back to him alive and well.’ 28At this he grew angry and would not go inside. His father came out and appealed to him. 29He replied to his father, ‘Listen! For all these years I have worked like a slave for you. Not once have I gone against your orders. And not once have you given me a young goat for a feast with my friends. 30But this son of yours has eaten up your property with prostitutes, and the moment he turns up, you slaughter the fattened calf for him!’ 31His father answered, ‘My child, you are with me always, and all that is mine belongs to you. 32But it was only right to celebrate and rejoice, for this brother of yours was dead and has come to life; he was lost and has been found.’”
fields.summary: When Pharisees and scribes grumble that Jesus welcomes sinners, Jesus tells of a lost sheep, a lost coin and a lost son. The father welcomes the younger son home and pleads with the resentful older son.

fields.title: Luke 16
fields.body_html:
A manager who acted shrewdly

1Jesus also told the disciples this: “A rich man had a manager, and word reached him that this man was squandering what he owned. 2So he sent for him and said, ‘What is this that I keep hearing about you? Hand in a report on how you have managed my affairs, because you cannot be my manager any longer.’ 3The manager thought it over: ‘My master is taking my position from me. What am I to do? Digging is too hard for me, and I would be ashamed to beg. 4Now I know what I will do, so that when I am put out of my job, people will open their homes to me.’ 5He sent for his master’s debtors one by one. To the first he said, ‘How much do you owe my master?’ 6‘About 600 gallons of olive oil,’ he answered. The manager told him, ‘Here is your bill. Sit down quickly and write 300 gallons.’ 7Then he said to another, ‘And what do you owe?’ ‘About 600 bushels of wheat,’ he replied. The manager told him, ‘Take your bill and write about 500.’ 8So the master gave the dishonest manager credit for acting so shrewdly. For the people of this age deal more shrewdly with others of their own kind than the people of the light do. 9And I tell you, use the wealth of this unjust world to make friends for yourselves, so that when it is gone, they will welcome you into the eternal homes.

10Someone who is faithful in the smallest matter is faithful in large matters too, and someone who is dishonest in the smallest matter is dishonest in large matters too. 11So if you have not been faithful in handling unjust wealth, who will put real wealth in your care? 12And if you have not proved faithful with what is another’s, who will hand you what is your own? 13No servant in a household can serve two masters. Either the servant will hate one master and love the other, or be loyal to one and look down on the other. You cannot serve both God and wealth.”

Lovers of money

14The Pharisees were listening to all this. They loved money, and they turned up their noses at him. 15He said to them, “You are the ones who make yourselves out to be righteous in front of people, but God knows your hearts. What people think highly of is loathsome in God’s sight.

16The law and the prophets lasted until John. From then on, the kingdom of God is announced as good news, and everyone is pressing their way into it.

17Yet heaven and earth will pass away more easily than one tiny stroke of the law will fall away.

18Any man who divorces his wife and marries someone else is committing adultery, and the man who marries a woman her husband has divorced is committing adultery too.

A rich man and a poor man named Lazarus

19There was once a rich man who wore purple and fine linen and feasted in great style day after day. 20And a poor man named Lazarus had been put down at his gate. His body was covered with sores, 21and he longed to fill his stomach with whatever dropped from the rich man’s table. Instead, the dogs would come and lick his sores. 22The day came when the poor man died, and angels carried him off to be at Abraham’s side. The rich man also died, and was given a burial. 23From Hades, in the midst of his torment, he raised his eyes and saw Abraham a long way off, and Lazarus close beside him. 24So he shouted, ‘Father Abraham, show me mercy! Send Lazarus here. Let him wet the end of his finger with water and cool my tongue, for this flame is causing me terrible pain.’ 25But Abraham answered, ‘My child, remember: while you were alive you had your good things, and Lazarus in the same way had the bad things. Now here he finds comfort, and you are suffering. 26What is more, a vast gulf lies fixed between us and you. Anyone who wanted to go across from here to you could not, and no one can cross from your side to ours.’ 27‘Then, father, I ask you this,’ he said. ‘Send him to my father’s house, 28where I have five brothers. He can give them a solemn warning, so that they do not come to this place of torment as well.’ 29But Abraham said, ‘Moses and the prophets are there for them. Let your brothers listen to what they say.’ 30He answered, ‘That is not enough, father Abraham. But if someone goes to them from among the dead, they will repent.’ 31Abraham said to him, ‘If they will not listen to Moses and the prophets, then even someone rising from the dead will not persuade them.’”
fields.summary: Jesus tells of a shrewd manager and teaches that no one can serve both God and money. The Pharisees, who love money, are warned, and Jesus tells of a rich man and a poor man named Lazarus.

fields.title: Luke 17
fields.body_html:
Stumbling, forgiveness and faith

1Jesus said to his disciples, “Things that trip people up and lead them into sin will certainly come. But how terrible for the one who brings them! 2It would be better for that person to be thrown into the sea with a millstone tied around their neck than to make one of these little ones stumble. 3Be on your guard. When your brother or sister does wrong, warn them. Then if they repent, forgive them. 4Seven times in one day they may wrong you, and seven times come back and say, ‘I repent.’ Even so, forgive them.”

5The apostles said to the Lord, “Give us more faith!” 6The Lord answered, “If you had faith the size of a mustard seed, you could tell this mulberry tree, ‘Tear yourself up by the roots and be planted in the sea,’ and it would do as you say.

Servants who only did their duty

7Imagine that one of you has a servant who has been out plowing or tending the sheep. When he comes in from the field, will you tell him, ‘Come straight in and take your place at the table’? 8Will you not tell him instead, ‘Make me something to eat. Then tie on your apron and serve me while I have my meal. You can eat and drink afterward’? 9The master does not owe the servant any thanks for doing what he was ordered to do, does he? 10It is the same with you. When you have done everything you were ordered to do, say, ‘We are unworthy servants. We have done no more than we were bound to do.’”

Ten healed, one returns

11As Jesus made his way toward Jerusalem, he went through the region between Samaria and Galilee. 12As he came into a village, ten men with leprosy came toward him. They kept their distance 13and called out loudly, “Jesus! Master! Have mercy on us!” 14Jesus saw them and told them, “Go and let the priests examine you.” On their way there, they were made clean. 15One of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, giving glory to God with a loud voice. 16He fell face down at the feet of Jesus, thanking him. And the man was a Samaritan. 17Jesus responded, “Ten men were made clean, were they not? So where are the other nine? 18Is this outsider the only one who came back to give glory to God?” 19Then he told him, “Stand up and go on your way. Your faith has made you well.”

Where the kingdom of God is

20Once the Pharisees asked Jesus when the kingdom of God would come. He answered them, “The kingdom of God does not come in a way you can watch for and track. 21People will not say, ‘It is here!’ or ‘It is over there!’ For the kingdom of God is among you.”

The day the Son of Man is revealed

22Then he said to the disciples, “There will be days when you ache to see even one day of the Son of Man, but you will not get to see it. 23People will tell you, ‘Look over there!’ or ‘Look here!’ Do not go out, and do not run after them. 24When lightning flashes, it lights up the sky from one edge to the other. That is how the Son of Man will be on his day. 25But before that, he must go through great suffering and be turned away by the people of this generation. 26What happened in Noah’s time will happen again in the days of the Son of Man. 27People were eating and drinking, taking wives and being given as wives, right up to the day Noah went into the ark. Then the flood came and wiped them all out. 28It was the same in Lot’s time. People ate and drank, bought and sold, planted and built. 29Then came the day Lot walked out of Sodom. Fire and sulfur fell like rain from heaven, and every one of them was destroyed. 30That is how it will be on the day when the Son of Man is revealed. 31On that day anyone up on the roof must not go down into the house to get their things. In the same way, anyone out in the field must not turn around to fetch what is behind. 32Remember Lot’s wife. 33Anyone who tries to hold on to their life will lose it, and anyone who loses it will keep it alive. 34I tell you, that night two people will be sleeping in one bed. One will be taken, and the other will be left behind. 35Two women will be grinding grain together. One will be taken, and the other will be left behind.” 37They asked him, “Where will this happen, Lord?” He said to them, “Where the corpse lies, there the vultures will flock together.”
fields.summary: Jesus teaches about causing others to stumble, forgiveness and faith. Of ten men healed of leprosy only a Samaritan returns to give thanks, and Jesus speaks of the kingdom of God and the day the Son of Man is revealed.

fields.title: Luke 18
fields.body_html:
A widow who kept coming

1Jesus told them a parable about their need to pray at all times and not lose heart. 2He said, “There was once a judge in a certain city who did not fear God and had no regard for anyone. 3In that city there was also a widow who came to him again and again. She said, ‘Give me my rights against my opponent.’ 4For a while he refused. But later he said to himself, ‘I do not fear God and I have no regard for anyone. 5Still, this widow is such a nuisance that I will give her justice. If I do not, she will keep coming until she wears me out.’” 6The Lord said, “Listen to what the unjust judge says. 7Then surely God will give justice to the people he has chosen, when they call out to him day and night. Will he be slow to help them? 8I tell you, he will see them vindicated, and without delay. Even so, when the Son of Man comes, will he find this kind of faith on the earth?” 9There were some who relied on themselves, sure that they were righteous, and who looked down on all others. Jesus told them this parable. 10“Two men went up to the temple to pray. One was a Pharisee, and the other was a tax collector. 11The Pharisee stood and prayed this prayer about himself: ‘God, I thank you that I am not like the rest of humanity, who are swindlers, crooks and adulterers, or even like this tax collector. 12Twice every week I fast, and I give a tenth of everything I take in.’ 13The tax collector, though, kept back at a distance and would not even lift his eyes toward heaven. Instead he struck his chest again and again and said, ‘God, be merciful to me, the sinner!’ 14I tell you, it was this man, not the other, who went home put right with God. For everyone who lifts themselves up will be brought low, and the one who takes the low place will be lifted up.”

Children and the kingdom

15People were even bringing their babies to him, so that he would touch them. The disciples saw it and began to scold them. 16But Jesus called them over and said, “Let the little children come to me, and do not try to stop them. The kingdom of God belongs to those who are like them. 17Truly I tell you, anyone who does not welcome the kingdom of God the way a child does will never get into it.”

A rich leader’s question

18One of the leaders asked him, “Good Teacher, what do I have to do to inherit eternal life?” 19Jesus answered, “Why are you calling me good? No one is good but God alone. 20You know the commandments: ‘Do not commit adultery. Do not murder. Do not steal. Do not give false testimony. Honor your father and your mother.’” 21The man replied, “I have kept every one of these from my youth.” 22Hearing this, Jesus told him, “You are still missing one thing. Sell all your possessions and hand out the money to the poor. Then you will have treasure in heaven. After that, come and follow me.” 23At these words the man was filled with sorrow, for he was a man of great wealth.

24Seeing this, Jesus said, “What a hard thing it is for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God! 25In fact, a camel could get through the eye of a needle more easily than a rich person could get into the kingdom of God.”

26Those listening asked, “Then who can be saved?” 27He answered, “What human beings cannot do is possible for God.”

28Peter said, “But we have given up what was ours and followed you!” 29He answered them, “Truly I tell you, anyone who has left a house, a wife, brothers, parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God 30is sure to be given back far more in this life, and in the age that is coming, eternal life.”

Going up to Jerusalem

31Taking the Twelve aside, he told them, “We are now going up to Jerusalem, and all that the prophets wrote about the Son of Man will come to pass. 32He will be given over to the Gentiles, who will make fun of him, treat him shamefully and spit on him. 33After whipping him they will put him to death, and on the third day he will rise.” 34But the Twelve understood none of this. What he said was hidden from them, and they did not grasp what he meant.

A blind man at Jericho sees

35Jesus was approaching Jericho. A blind man was sitting there beside the road, begging. 36He heard a crowd passing by and asked what it was all about. 37They told him, “Jesus of Nazareth is going by.” 38So he shouted, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!” 39The people at the front of the crowd told him sternly to be quiet, but he cried out all the louder, “Son of David, have mercy on me!” 40Jesus stood still and gave orders for them to bring the man to him. When the man came near, Jesus asked him, 41“What would you like me to do for you?” He answered, “Lord, I want to see again.” 42Jesus told him, “See again. Your faith has made you well.” 43At once he could see, and he followed him, giving glory to God. All the people saw what happened, and they gave praise to God.
fields.summary: Jesus tells of a widow who would not stop asking and of a Pharisee and a tax collector praying in the temple. Jesus welcomes the children, answers a rich leader, foretells death and rising, and gives sight to a blind man near Jericho.

fields.title: Luke 19
fields.body_html:
Zacchaeus climbs a tree

1Jesus entered Jericho and was making his way through the town. 2A man named Zacchaeus lived there. He was a chief tax collector, and he was rich. 3He was trying to see who Jesus was, but he could not see over the crowd, because he was a short man. 4So he ran on ahead and climbed a sycamore-fig tree to see him, since Jesus was going to come along that road. 5When Jesus reached the spot, he looked up and said to him, “Zacchaeus, hurry down. Today is the day I have to stay in your home.” 6So he hurried down and gladly welcomed him. 7Everyone who saw it began to mutter and complain. “He has gone to be a guest at the house of a sinner!” they said. 8But Zacchaeus stood up and said to the Lord, “Lord, see: half of what I own I am giving to the poor. And if I have taken anything from anyone by cheating, I am paying it back four times over.” 9Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this household. This man too is one of Abraham’s sons. 10The Son of Man came to look for what was lost and to save it.”

Ten servants and ten minas

11As they listened to this, Jesus went on to tell them a parable. He did this because he was near Jerusalem, and they supposed that the kingdom of God was about to appear at once. 12So he said, “A man from a noble family traveled to a faraway country to be made king there, and then to come back home. 13Before he left, he called ten of his servants and gave them ten minas, one to each. ‘Put this money to work until I come back,’ he told them. 14But the people of his country hated him. They sent a delegation after him to say, ‘We do not want this man to be our king.’ 15He was made king and came back home. Then he sent for the servants to whom he had given the money, to find out what profit each had made by his trading. 16The first came and said, ‘Master, your mina has made ten minas more.’ 17‘Excellent, good servant!’ he replied. ‘You have been trustworthy in a very small matter, so you will have authority over ten cities.’ 18The second came and said, ‘Master, your mina has earned five minas.’ 19To him too he said, ‘You will be over five cities.’ 20Then another came and said, ‘Master, here is your mina. I kept it put away in a piece of cloth. 21I was afraid of you, because you are a severe man. You take out what you never put in, and you harvest what you never planted.’ 22He answered, ‘Your own words condemn you, you wicked servant! So you knew that I am a severe man, taking out what I never put in and harvesting what I never planted? 23Then why did you not put my money in the bank? Then when I came back, I would have collected it with interest.’ 24Then he said to those standing there, ‘Take the mina from him and give it to the one who has ten.’ 25‘Master,’ they said, ‘he has ten minas already!’ 26‘I tell you, everyone who has will be given more. But the one who has nothing will lose even what they have. 27As for these enemies of mine who did not want me as their king, bring them here and execute them in my presence.’”

The king comes riding on a colt

28After saying this, Jesus went on ahead of them, going up to Jerusalem.

29As he came near Bethphage and Bethany, by the hill called the Mount of Olives, he sent off two of the disciples. 30“Go to the village ahead of you,” he told them. “As you go into it, you will find a young donkey tied there, one that nobody has ever ridden. Untie it and bring it here. 31If anyone asks you, ‘Why are you untying it?’ tell them, ‘The Lord needs it.’” 32Those who had been sent went off and found things just as he had told them. 33As they were untying the young donkey, its owners asked them, “Why are you untying the donkey?” 34They answered, “The Lord needs it.” 35They brought the donkey to Jesus, threw their cloaks over it, and helped Jesus get on. 36As he rode along, people spread their cloaks on the road. 37As he came close to the city, where the road goes down the Mount of Olives, the whole crowd of his disciples began to praise God joyfully and loudly for all the mighty deeds they had seen. 38They shouted, “Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!” 39Some Pharisees in the crowd said to him, “Teacher, tell your disciples to stop!” 40He answered, “I tell you, if these people were silent, the very stones would shout.”

Jesus weeps over Jerusalem

41When he came nearer and saw the city, he wept over it. 42“If only you too had known on this day the things that lead to peace!” he said. “But now they are hidden from your sight. 43For a time is coming for you when your enemies will build a siege wall against you. They will encircle you and press in on you from all sides. 44They will level you to the ground, you and your children inside you. They will leave no stone on top of another within you, because you did not recognize the time when God came to visit you.”

A house of prayer

45Then Jesus went into the temple and began to throw out the people who were selling there. 46He said to them, “Scripture says, ‘My house will be a house of prayer.’ But you have turned it into a hideout for robbers.”

47Every day he taught in the temple. The chief priests and the scribes wanted to kill him, and so did the leaders of the people. 48But they could find no way to do it, because all the people clung to him, listening to every word.
fields.summary: In Jericho Zacchaeus climbs a tree to see Jesus and becomes a changed man. Jesus tells of ten servants entrusted with minas, rides into Jerusalem on a colt, weeps over the city and drives the traders out of the temple.

fields.title: Luke 20
fields.body_html:
A question about authority

1One day, as Jesus was teaching the people in the temple and telling them the good news, the chief priests and the scribes came up to him, together with the elders. 2“Tell us,” they said to him, “what authority do you have to do these things? Who is it that gave you this authority?” 3He answered them, “I too will ask you a question. Tell me this: 4John’s baptism: did it come from heaven, or from people?” 5They discussed it among themselves and said, “If we answer, ‘From heaven,’ he will ask, ‘Then why did you not believe him?’ 6But if we answer, ‘From people,’ the whole crowd will stone us, because they are sure John was a prophet.” 7So they answered that they did not know where it came from. 8Jesus said to them, “Then I am not going to tell you either by what authority I do these things.”

The tenant farmers and the owner’s son

9Then he told the people this parable: “A man planted a vineyard and let it out to tenants. Then he went abroad and stayed away a long while. 10When harvest time came, he sent a servant to the tenants to collect his share of the vineyard’s crop. But the tenants beat him and sent him back with nothing. 11So he sent a second servant, but they beat this one as well, insulted him, and sent him off with nothing. 12Then he sent a third, and they wounded this one and threw him out. 13Then the master of the vineyard said, ‘What am I to do? I will send my son, the one I love. It may be that they will show him respect.’ 14But the tenants saw him coming and talked it over among themselves. ‘This is the one who will inherit,’ they said to each other. ‘If we kill him, the property will be ours.’ 15So they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. So what will the master of the vineyard do to them? 16He will come and put these tenants to death, and give the vineyard to others.” Hearing this, the people cried out, “May that never happen!” 17Jesus looked straight at them and said, “Then what is the meaning of the words that are written, ‘The stone the builders discarded has become the main stone at the corner’? 18All who fall on that stone will be smashed, and if it falls on someone, it will grind that person to dust.” 19The scribes and the chief priests wanted to get their hands on him then and there, but they were afraid of the people. They understood that he had aimed this parable at them.

Paying tribute to Caesar

20They watched him closely and sent agents who played the part of honest, devout men. Their aim was to seize on some word of his and use it to deliver him into the governor’s power and jurisdiction. 21So they put a question to him: “Teacher, we are sure that you are correct in what you say and teach. No one’s rank sways you, and you teach the way of God with truth. 22Does the law allow us to pay tribute to Caesar, or not?” 23But he saw through their trickery and said to them, 24“Let me see a denarius. Whose likeness and whose inscription does it carry?” They answered, “Caesar’s.” 25He said to them, “Then pay back to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and to God what belongs to God.” 26So with the people looking on, they found nothing in his words to seize on. His answer left them amazed, and they had nothing more to say.

A question about the resurrection

27Then some Sadducees came up, men who say there is no resurrection, and put a question to him: 28“Teacher, Moses gave us this law in writing: when someone’s brother dies married but without children, the surviving brother is to marry the widow and raise children for the one who died. 29There were once seven brothers. The first married and died without having a child. 30Then the second 31and the third married her, and so on with all seven: each one died and left no children. 32Last of all, the woman died too. 33So when the dead rise, whose wife will she be? All seven of them had her as a wife.”

34Jesus answered them, “In this age, men take wives and women are given to husbands. 35But those who are judged worthy to have a share in the age to come and in the rising from the dead neither take wives nor are given to husbands. 36They will never die again, for they are equal to the angels; and having had their share in the resurrection, they are children of God. 37And that the dead are raised, even Moses made plain in the account of the burning bush, where he calls the Lord ‘the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob.’ 38God is not a God of dead people but of living people, since all of them live in relation to him.” 39Some of the scribes responded, “Teacher, that was a fine answer.” 40From then on they did not dare put any more questions to him.

David’s son and David’s Lord

41Then he said to them, “How can people say that Christ is the son of David? 42David himself says in the book of Psalms, ‘The Lord said to my Lord: “Take your seat at my right hand 43until I put your enemies under your feet as a footstool.”‘ 44So if David calls him ‘Lord,’ how can he be David’s son?” 45In the hearing of all the people, he said to the disciples, 46“Be on your guard against the scribes. They like to parade in long robes. They love it when people greet them in the marketplaces, and they love the front seats in the synagogues and the best couches at dinners. 47They swallow up the property of widows, and they pray at great length to cover it up. These men will receive the heavier judgment.”
fields.summary: The leaders question Jesus’s authority, and Jesus tells of the tenant farmers who killed the owner’s son. Jesus answers questions about paying tribute to Caesar and about the resurrection, and asks how David’s son can be David’s Lord.

fields.title: Luke 21
fields.body_html:
A poor widow’s gift

1Jesus looked up and watched as rich people dropped their gifts into the temple’s offering chests. 2He also noticed a needy widow drop in two pennies. 3Then he said, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has given more than all the rest. 4Every one of them gave out of their surplus. But she, out of her need, has given the whole of what she had to live on.”

Not one stone on another

5Some people were talking about the temple: how fine its stones were, and how it was decorated with gifts given to God. Jesus said, 6“You are looking at all this. But days are coming when it will all be torn down, and not a stone will stay standing on another.”

7They put a question to him: “Teacher, when will these things be? And what sign will there be when they are about to take place?” 8He answered, “Take care that no one leads you astray. Many will come claiming my name and saying, ‘I am the one!’ and, ‘The time has come near!’ Do not go after them. 9When you hear about wars and rebellions, do not panic. All this has to happen first, but it does not mean that the end comes at once.” 10Then he went on to tell them, “One nation will go to war with another, and one kingdom with another. 11There will be powerful earthquakes, and in place after place famines and diseases. Fearful things will happen, and great signs will appear in the sky.

12Before all that, however, they will arrest you and hunt you down. They will hand you over to synagogues and to prisons, and you will be led off to stand before kings and governors for the sake of my name. 13This will give you the chance to bear witness. 14So settle it in your hearts: do not plan your defense in advance. 15I myself will give you the words and the wisdom to speak, and not one of your opponents will be able to stand against them or argue back. 16You will be handed over even by your own parents and brothers and sisters, your relatives and your friends, and some of you they will kill. 17You will be hated by everyone on account of my name. 18Yet not a single hair of your head will be lost. 19Hold out to the end, and so win your lives.

Jerusalem surrounded

20When you see Jerusalem with armies encamped all around it, then be sure that it will soon be laid waste. 21Then people in Judea should run for the hills. Those inside the city should leave it, and those out in the fields should not go back in. 22For these are the days of punishment, when everything that is written will come true. 23How terrible it will be in those days for women who are pregnant or nursing a baby! Great hardship will come on the land, and wrath on this people. 24They will be cut down by the sword and carried off as captives to every nation. Jerusalem will be trampled underfoot by the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles have run their course.

The Son of Man comes in a cloud

25Signs will appear in the sun, the moon and the stars. On the earth whole nations will be gripped with distress, not knowing where to turn as the sea roars and heaves. 26Fear will drain the strength out of people as they wait for what is coming on the world, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken. 27And then people will see the Son of Man come in a cloud with power and with great glory. 28As soon as these things start to happen, straighten up and look up, for the day of your redemption is almost here.”

Learn from the fig tree

29He told them a parable: “Look at the fig tree, and at all the trees. 30Once they burst into leaf, you only need to look at them to know that summer is near. 31It is the same with you. When you see these things happening, be sure of this: the kingdom of God is near. 32Truly I tell you, all of this will happen before this generation is gone. 33Heaven and earth will disappear, but my words will last forever.

Stay awake and pray

34Be on your guard. Do not let your hearts grow dull with wild parties and drinking and the worries of everyday life, or that day will catch you off guard, 35like a trap that snaps shut. It will come on everyone who lives anywhere on earth. 36Keep watch at all times, and pray for strength to come safely through all that is going to happen, and to stand before the Son of Man.”

37By day Jesus was teaching in the temple. At night he would go out of the city and spend the night on the hill known as the Mount of Olives. 38At dawn all the people would come to him in the temple to listen.
fields.summary: Jesus praises a poor widow’s gift and foretells the temple’s fall, Jerusalem surrounded by armies, and the Son of Man coming in a cloud. The disciples are to learn from the fig tree and stay awake and pray.

fields.title: Luke 22
fields.body_html:
The leaders plot, and Judas joins them

1Now the time was drawing near for the feast of Unleavened Bread, which is known as the Passover. 2The chief priests and the scribes were looking for some way to put him to death, because they were afraid of the people.

3Then Satan entered into Judas, the one called Iscariot, who was one of the Twelve. 4He went off and talked with the chief priests and the temple officers about how he could betray him to them. 5They were glad and agreed to pay him money. 6He accepted, and from then on he looked for a good chance to betray him to them when no crowd was around.

Preparing the Passover

7Then came the day of Unleavened Bread, the day when the Passover lamb had to be killed as a sacrifice. 8So Jesus sent Peter and John with these instructions: “Go and get the Passover meal ready for us to eat.” 9They asked him, “Where do you want us to get it ready?” 10He told them, “As you go into the city, you will be met by a man who is carrying a jar of water. Follow him into whatever house he goes into. 11Say to the owner of the house, ‘The Teacher asks you, “Which is the guest room where I can eat the Passover with my disciples?”‘ 12He will show you a large room upstairs, with everything laid out. Get the meal ready there.” 13So they went off and found it all just as he had said, and they got the Passover ready.

The Passover meal with the apostles

14When the hour came, he took his place at the table, and the apostles with him. 15And he said to them, “How I have longed to eat this Passover with you before I suffer! 16For I tell you, I will not eat it again until it finds its fulfillment in the kingdom of God.” 17Then he took a cup, gave thanks, and said, “Take this and share it among yourselves. 18I tell you, from now on I will not drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes.” 19Then he took bread, and after giving thanks he broke it and handed it to them, saying, “This is my body, which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of me.” 20In the same way he took the cup after the meal, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood, poured out for you. 21Yet the hand of the man who is betraying me is here with me on the table. 22The Son of Man is going the way that has been marked out for him. But how terrible it will be for that man who betrays him!” 23They began to ask one another which of them it could possibly be who was going to do such a thing.

The greatest is the one who serves

24A quarrel also broke out among them over which of them was to be thought the greatest. 25But he said to them, “The kings of the Gentiles act as lords over their people, and those who hold power over them are given the title ‘Benefactor’. 26With you it must not be this way. Instead, the greatest among you must become like the youngest, and the one in charge like the one who waits on others. 27Think about it: who is greater, the guest who lies at the table, or the one who serves the meal? Surely the one at the table. Yet here I am among you as the one who serves.

28You are the ones who have stood by me through my trials. 29And just as my Father has granted me a kingdom, so I grant one to you. 30You will eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and you will sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel. 31Simon, Simon, Satan has demanded to have all of you, to sift you like wheat. 32But I have prayed for you, so that your faith will not give out. And you, once you have turned back, must strengthen your brothers.” 33Peter answered him, “Lord, I am ready to go to prison with you, and even to die with you.” 34Jesus replied, “I tell you, Peter, before a rooster crows today, you will have said three times that you do not know me.”

Purse, bag and sword

35Then he said to them, “When I sent you out with no money bag, no traveler’s bag and no sandals, were you short of anything?” They said, “Not a thing.” 36He said to them, “But now, whoever has a money bag must take it along, and a traveler’s bag too. And whoever has no sword should sell their cloak and buy one. 37For I tell you, what is written must be fulfilled in me: ‘He was counted among the lawless.’ Yes, what was written about me is reaching its end.” 38They said, “Lord, look, here are two swords.” And he said to them, “That is enough.”

Not my will but yours

39Then he left and went, as was his habit, to the Mount of Olives, and the disciples went with him. 40When he arrived at the place, he said to them, “Pray that you do not come into temptation.” 41Then he went off from them about a stone’s throw, knelt down, and began to pray, 42“Father, if you are willing, remove this cup from me. Yet let your will be done, not mine.” 43Then an angel from heaven appeared to him and gave him strength. 44In his anguish he prayed all the more intensely, and his sweat became like thick drops of blood dripping down onto the ground. 45When he got up from prayer and came back to the disciples, he found them asleep, worn down by their grief. 46And he said to them, “Why are you sleeping? Get up and pray, so that you will not come into temptation.”

Judas comes with a crowd

47While he was still speaking, a crowd appeared. The man called Judas, one of the Twelve, was leading them, and he came up to Jesus to kiss him. 48But Jesus said to him, “Judas, is it with a kiss that you betray the Son of Man?” 49When those around him saw what was going to happen, they said, “Lord, should we strike with our swords?” 50And one of them struck the high priest’s servant and cut off his right ear. 51But Jesus said, “Enough of this!” And he touched the man’s ear and healed him. 52Then Jesus said to the chief priests, the officers of the temple guard and the elders who had come out against him, “Did you have to come out with swords and clubs, as if I were a bandit? 53Day after day I was with you in the temple, and you did not lift a hand against me. But this is your hour, and the power of darkness.”

Peter’s three denials

54They seized him, led him away and brought him into the high priest’s house. Peter followed at a distance. 55People had lit a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down around it, and Peter sat among them. 56A servant girl saw him sitting in the firelight. She stared at him and said, “This man was with him too.” 57But he denied it. “Woman, I do not know him,” he said. 58A little later someone else saw him and said, “You are one of them too.” But Peter said, “Friend, I am not.” 59About an hour later another man insisted, “This is the truth: this fellow was with him. He is a Galilean too.” 60But Peter said, “Friend, I have no idea what you are talking about.” At that very moment, while he was still speaking, a rooster crowed. 61And the Lord turned and looked at Peter. Then Peter remembered the Lord’s words, how he had told him, “Today, before a rooster crows, you will deny me three times.” 62He went outside and wept bitterly.

Blindfolded and mocked

63The men who were guarding Jesus made fun of him as they beat him. 64They covered his eyes and kept asking him, “Prophesy! Who was it that struck you?” 65And they said many other insulting things against him.

Questioned by the council

66At daybreak the elders of the people met together, both chief priests and scribes, and they took him away to their council. 67They said, “If you are the Christ, tell us.” But he said to them, “If I tell you, you will not believe. 68And if I ask you a question, you will not answer. 69But from now on the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God.” 70They all said, “So you are the Son of God?” He answered them, “You say that I am.” 71Then they said, “Why do we need any more witnesses? We have heard it ourselves from his own mouth.”
fields.summary: Judas agrees to hand Jesus over, and at the Passover meal Jesus gives the bread and the cup to the apostles and teaches that the greatest is the one who serves. Jesus prays on the Mount of Olives, is arrested, denied three times by Peter, mocked and questioned by the council.

fields.title: Luke 23
fields.body_html:
Jesus is brought to Pilate

1Then the whole assembly got up and brought him before Pilate. 2They started to bring charges against him: “We have found this man leading our nation astray. He forbids paying taxes to Caesar, and he claims to be Christ, a king.” 3So Pilate asked him, “Are you the king of the Jews?” He answered him, “You say so.” 4Pilate told the chief priests and the crowds, “I find this man guilty of nothing.” 5But they pressed the charge harder: “He is stirring up the people with his teaching all over Judea. He started in Galilee and has come all the way here.” 6When Pilate heard this, he asked whether the man was from Galilee. 7When he learned that he came under Herod’s authority, he sent him on to Herod, who was also in Jerusalem at that time. 8Herod was delighted when he saw Jesus. He had wanted to see him for a long time because of what he had heard about him, and he hoped to watch him perform some sign. 9He put question after question to him, but Jesus gave him no answer at all. 10The chief priests and the scribes stood by, accusing him fiercely. 11Herod and his soldiers treated him with scorn and made fun of him. Herod had him dressed in a bright robe and sent him back to Pilate. 12That same day Herod and Pilate became friends. Until then there had been hostility between them. 13Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers and the people 14and said to them, “You brought this man before me on the charge that he was turning the people from their loyalty. I have questioned him in your presence, and I have found him guilty of none of the things you accuse him of. 15Neither did Herod, for he sent him back to us. Plainly he has done nothing that deserves death. 16So I will have him flogged and then let him go.”

The crowd asks for Barabbas

18But the whole crowd shouted as one, “Take this man away! Set Barabbas free for us!” 19He had been put in prison for a riot that broke out in the city, and for murder. 20Pilate spoke to them once more, because he wanted to set Jesus free. 21But they kept shouting back, “Crucify him! Crucify him!” 22For the third time he said to them, “Why? What wrong has this man done? I have found no reason to put him to death. So I will have him flogged and then let him go.” 23But they pressed their demand with loud shouts, calling for him to be crucified, and their shouting won the day. 24So Pilate ruled that what they asked for should be done. 25He set free the man they asked for, the one who had been put in prison for revolt and murder. But Jesus he gave up to them to do as they wished.

On the way to the Skull

26As they led him away, they took hold of a man named Simon from Cyrene, who was coming in from the countryside. They laid the cross on him and made him carry it behind Jesus.

27A large crowd of the people followed him, among them women who were mourning and wailing for him. 28Jesus turned toward them and said, “Daughters of Jerusalem, it is not me you should be weeping over. Weep over yourselves and over your children. 29Days are coming when people will say, ‘Blessed are the women who could not have children, the wombs that never gave birth and the breasts that never fed a baby.’ 30Then they will start saying to the mountains, ‘Fall on us!’ and to the hills, ‘Cover us!’ 31For if this is how they treat wood that is green, what will become of wood that is dry?” 32Two other men, both criminals, were also led out with him to be executed. 33When they reached the place called the Skull, they crucified him there, with the criminals, one at his right hand and one at his left. 34Jesus kept saying, “Father, forgive them. They do not know what they are doing.” They shared out his clothes among themselves by casting lots. 35The people stood there looking on. The rulers joined in the scoffing. “He saved others,” they said. “So let him save himself, if this man is God’s Christ, the one God chose.” 36The soldiers made fun of him as well. They came up and held out sour wine to him, 37saying, “If you are the king of the Jews, save yourself!” 38Above him there was also a written notice: “This is the king of the Jews.”

The two criminals

39One of the criminals hanging beside him kept abusing him. “You are the Christ, are you not? Then save yourself, and us too!” 40But the other criminal rebuked him: “Have you no fear even of God, when you are under the same sentence of death? 41For us it is fair: we are paying the due price for what we did. But this man has done nothing amiss.” 42Then he said, “Jesus, remember me when you come in your kingdom.” 43Jesus answered him, “Truly I tell you, this very day you will be with me in paradise.”

Darkness at midday and Jesus’ last words

44It was already about midday when darkness covered the whole land, and it lasted until three in the afternoon. 45The light of the sun failed, and the curtain in the sanctuary was torn down the middle. 46Then Jesus cried out in a loud voice, “Father, I place my spirit in your hands.” With these words he breathed out his last breath.

47The centurion saw what had taken place, and he gave glory to God, saying, “Truly this man was righteous.” 48All the crowds who had gathered to watch this spectacle saw what had happened, and they turned back home, striking their breasts. 49Everyone who knew him stood far off. The women who had come with him from Galilee were standing there too, and they saw these things.

Joseph lays Jesus in a tomb

50There was a man named Joseph who was a member of the council, a good and righteous man 51who had not given his consent to what the council planned and did. He came from Arimathea, a town of the Jews, and he was waiting for the kingdom of God. 52He went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus. 53He took the body down from the cross and wrapped it in a linen sheet. Then he laid him in a tomb cut out of the rock, where no one had ever been buried. 54It was the day of Preparation, and the Sabbath was drawing near. 55The women who had come with him from Galilee went after Joseph. They saw the tomb and the way his body was laid there. 56Then they went back and got spices and fragrant oils ready.

On the Sabbath they rested, as the commandment required.
